tests_note: The table was built by reading the two test suites, never by running them. No coverage numbers were measured.

tests.label: Refusing to overwrite coyomap's own map
tests.gap: Nothing exercises the refusal that protects the coyomap clone's own map. A build started in the wrong folder could overwrite it.

tests.label: Refusing to read coyomap's own map by mistake

tests.why: Every map reader among the build commands passes through the refusal.
The refusal prints one plain line, never a crash dump.
Someone mapping coyomap itself can still switch the refusal off.

tests.gap: Three commands are driven for real. The rest are covered only by a scan of the source text.

tests.label: Turning away a request that names another machine

tests.why: The name check accepts this machine and refuses every other name.

tests.gap: No test sends a real request carrying a foreign name. A wiring slip in the map server would go unnoticed.

tests.label: Guard on requests that change the project list
tests.gap: No test ever sends a change request to the map server. A web page you visit could edit your project list.

tests.label: Adding, dropping and reordering remembered projects

tests.why: The remembered project list adds, removes, de-duplicates and survives a restart.
A new order for the remembered projects is saved and read back.

tests.gap: The three network addresses that drive those changes are never called. Only the storage under them is tested.

tests.label: Listing any folder on this machine

tests.why: Folder listing marks each folder that already holds a map.

tests.gap: The address the browser calls is never exercised. Nothing checks the answer for a folder that does not exist.

tests.label: Health answer naming the pinned commit
tests.gap: No test asks the map server whether it is answering. A break there shows only as a page that never loads.

tests.label: Serving one file's text at the pinned commit

tests.why: One file's text is served at the pinned commit and at another commit.
Ignored files, the version-control folder and paths that climb out are refused.
A path that climbs above the project folder is rejected.

tests.gap: No test feeds a file big enough to hit the size limit. A limit that stopped working shows only as a stalled page.

tests.label: Closing sequence that ships a build

tests.why: The closing sequence lists its steps in the order the method sets.
A failing step stops the run and names the steps left undone.

tests.gap: Every step runs against a stand-in, never the real command. A change inside one command can still break the sequence.

tests.label: One pre-commit verdict over every check

tests.why: A clean map succeeds and writes both of its reports.
A blocking problem fails the run and is recorded as blocking.
A check that never ran can never be reported as clean.
A faked count of challenged claims is caught by recomputing it.

tests.gap: The suite feeds hand-built maps. No test runs the verdict over a map a real build just produced.

tests.label: Honesty record of what the doubters challenged

tests.why: Verdict files are checked for shape, folded into votes and written back.
Each element gets the review outcome the votes actually support.

tests.gap: Nothing checks the record against a full real build's verdict files.

tests.label: Editing map rows in one all-or-nothing write

tests.why: Two corrections landing on one row are both refused, so nothing half-lands.
A conflicting duplicate is reported and no change is written.
An edit that would split a merged row is refused.

tests.gap: No test interrupts a write midway. A crash during the write is not covered.

tests.label: Merging the build agents' fragments into one map

tests.why: Merging the stored fragments gives the same bytes every time.
Every stored fragment passes the self-check a build agent runs.
Conflicts, duplicates and missing pieces across fragments are resolved or reported.
A fragment with invented ids or bad wording is refused before merging.

tests.gap: The stored fragment set is one project's. A shape only another project produces would not be met.

tests.label: Checks a map must pass to be well formed

tests.why: Four hundred cases cover shape, story, rule, wiring and data checks.
Places where a map contradicts itself are found and reported.
Deliberately broken maps are caught rather than passed.

tests.gap: A check that is too loose still passes its own test. Only the trap maps push back on that.

tests.label: Survey of the code a build starts from

tests.why: The survey walks the files, names the symbols and counts the sizes.
Directory expectations and size bands come out at the right grain.
Only files version control tracks are walked.

tests.gap: The survey reads fifteen languages. Tests feed only Python and JavaScript, so thirteen parsers are unproven.

tests.label: Leaving named code off the map

tests.why: Ignored paths drop out of the survey, the file tree and the counts.

tests.gap: No test runs a whole build with an ignore list and checks the printed counts.

tests.label: Assigning code to groups and balancing the diagrams

tests.why: Path rules expand into an explicit assignment for every file.
Diagrams holding too many boxes are named with a suggested split.

tests.gap: Balance is judged on small hand-built maps. Nothing checks the advice on a map the size of a real project.

tests.label: Map data shape, shared words and schema

tests.why: Every part of a map loads, saves and round-trips without loss.
The fixed word lists stay closed and agree with the model.
The published schema still matches the data shape it describes.
Notes headings are read into the sections a map stores.

tests.gap: The schema check compares shapes. Nothing validates a real map file against the schema itself.

tests.label: Briefing that tells a build what to read

tests.why: The list of files a build will read is produced before it starts.
Each helper agent's brief is printed complete and with the right ids.

tests.gap: No test proves a brief a helper agent receives is one it can actually follow.

tests.label: Build log of sessions and slice timings

tests.why: The session that built a map is stamped and listed back.
What each build slice took is recorded and sorted longest first.

tests.gap: Nothing checks the log after a real build. Only hand-written entries are read back.

tests.label: Report of what a code change did to the map

tests.why: A change between two commits is matched to the map parts it touches.
A hit on one box spreads to the boxes and steps that depend on it.
The report also comes back correctly over the network.

tests.gap: Repositories in the tests are tiny. A change touching hundreds of files is never tried.

tests.label: Every command surviving a realistic map

tests.why: A new command cannot ship without joining the sweep that runs it.
Every command runs against a real map without crashing.
Every command refuses an option it does not know.
No command hangs waiting for a person to type.

tests.gap: The map server is the one command left out, because starting it blocks. Its behaviour is checked elsewhere.

tests.label: Restarting the map server when the viewer changes
tests.gap: Nothing tests the watcher that restarts the map server. A silent failure leaves developers looking at stale screens.

tests.label: Archiving a map with the conversation that built it
tests.gap: Nothing tests the backup that moves a map and its chat aside. A bug there loses work with no warning.

tests.label: File tree marked by how far the map covers it

tests.why: Folders and files come back marked by how much of the map reaches them.

tests.gap: The tree is built from small fixtures. A repository with deep nesting is not tried.

tests.label: Turning a map into diagrams and cards

tests.why: Each view's diagram and text are produced from the stored map.
Boxes land in the right groups and lanes on every picture.
Processes, queues and the arrows between them are drawn correctly.
Each feature's facts are gathered from the flows that reach it.

tests.gap: The pictures are checked as data, not as drawings. A layout that overlaps still passes.

tests.label: Screen addresses and the trail back

tests.why: A reload comes back to the exact screen you were on.
Going back walks the real screens you visited.
A broken or stale link still draws a page with a trail.

tests.gap: Eight kinds of address open a screen. Only the feature, actor and use case ones are opened in a browser.

tests.label: Feature, happy path and actor pages

tests.why: The happy path draws one line, broken where the person changes.
Feature boxes are equal height and the line bridges the gaps.
An actor's board says where each use case happens.

tests.gap: Coverage is measured on one stored map. A product with very many features is not drawn in a test.

tests.label: Interfaces and rules pages

tests.why: Each interface card says what kind of thing it is.
Every interface draws one plain line to the product.
One shared section index builds every card page, the rules page included.

tests.gap: Interfaces are checked in a real browser. The rules page is only read as text, so nothing proves it draws.

tests.label: Storage, tests and system pages

tests.why: Each stored record's box carries where it lives and how it changes.
Coverage rows reach the browser with their targets resolved to names.
The system page is built as cards over one shared builder.

tests.gap: No test opens the storage page or the coverage page in a browser. Both are checked only as data.

tests.label: Code column beside the map

tests.why: Opening a use case opens the code column once, then leaves it alone.
Opening the code column narrows the picture instead of breaking it.

tests.gap: Nothing tests the code text itself, its colouring, or the side-by-side view of a change.

tests.label: Search across everything the map holds

tests.why: A feature found by search lands on its own card.
A search result can be pinned in the picture it belongs to.

tests.gap: Search is exercised outside a browser. Nothing proves the box opens, filters and closes on screen.

tests.label: Screen for exploring a change report
tests.gap: Nothing tests the screen that shows what a code change did. Its data is checked, its screen is not.

tests.label: Cards, canvas and clicking a box

tests.why: A selected box gets a card joined to it by a line.
A box name opens the thing and its frame selects the box.
The inspector answers with the record the map actually stores.
A drawing squeezed to nothing recovers instead of staying broken.

tests.gap: The written rule for what a card may show is never checked against the code that draws it.

tests.label: Viewer look in both light and dark

tests.why: A board that scrolls sideways shades the edge where more content sits.
A pinned section bar casts its shadow only once it is stuck.

tests.gap: Only a handful of styling rules are measured on screen. Colour and dark mode are never checked.

tests.label: Reader settings kept in the browser
tests.gap: Eight saved settings decide how source links open and how panels sit. No test reads or writes any of them.

tests.label: Opening the code behind a box in your own editor
tests.gap: Nothing tests the editor link, the code host link, or the check that refuses an unsafe link. A bad link opens whatever it names.

tests.label: Installing coyomap into a coding agent

tests.why: The install steps cover every skill the project offers.
Each skill points only at its own entry document.

tests.gap: Only the install text is read. Nothing performs an install and then checks the command works.

tests.label: Building a project's first map, end to end

tests.why: Every check reads a freshly merged map without crashing.
Each build command runs against a realistic map.

tests.gap: No test drives a whole build from source code to a finished map. The agent's part cannot run in the suite.

tests.label: Folding a change into the map and re-checking it

tests.why: Corrections land on the right rows or are refused with a reason.
Two maps of the same work are compared row by row.

tests.gap: Single edits are covered. Nothing walks the whole path from a change report to an accepted map.

tests.label: Scoring a map and comparing it with the accepted one

tests.why: Every measurement taken from a map is computed and checked.
The verdict follows the bands, and a worse hard check blocks.
Rule counts and rule sites are measured and banded.
Scoring, comparing and judging run together on one map.

tests.gap: The bands come from stored settings. No test proves today's bands are the right width.

tests.label: Judging a run and testing the doubters

tests.why: Marks and votes fold into one report with a stated verdict.
A scoring run produces its files and files them in the right place.
Planted false claims are produced and the catches are counted.

tests.gap: The judging inputs are hand-built. Nothing scores a run made by a real agent.

tests.label: Finding relations a rebuild dropped

tests.why: Arrows the old map had and the new one lost are listed.

tests.gap: Loss is judged between two stored maps. Nothing checks the finding against the code itself.

tests.label: Moving a map aside before a rebuild

tests.why: The whole map moves and nothing is deleted.
A move that fails partway puts everything back.
A rehearsal run writes nothing at all.

tests.gap: Nothing tests two of these moves running at the same time on one project.

tests.label: Reading a build's chat and scoring how it went

tests.why: A build's chat log is read in slices, with its commands and results.
Time and tokens for one build are counted and divided correctly.
Two hundred and fifty cases score how the build agent behaved.
A build that has not finished is reported instead of reviewed.
A review's finished rows are checked against the code history.
Numbers the tools state about a live map are re-measured.

tests.gap: One small stored chat stands in for a real build. Shapes only a long build produces are untried.

tests.label: Every method-quality command surviving real inputs

tests.why: A new command cannot ship without joining the sweep that runs it.
Every command runs against a real map and a real chat log.
The sweep leaves the stored inputs exactly as it found them.

tests.gap: The sweep only checks a command runs. What each command answers is checked elsewhere.

tests.label: Instructions saying what a map must contain

tests.why: The instructions stay consistent with the commands they tell an agent to run.
Long sentences, code names and dashes in map text are counted.

tests.gap: The checks read structure and names. No test proves an agent following the instructions produces a good map.

tests.label: Instructions saying how a build runs

tests.why: Each phase names commands that exist and flags they accept.
Each helper agent's brief is printed with the right ids and rules.

tests.gap: Only what the instructions say is checked. Whether a build actually follows them is measured by hand later.

tests.label: Model spec, worker briefs and regression checks

tests.why: The written model spec agrees with the data shape the tools load.
Every worker brief is complete and names only real ids.
Each armed regression check is dated and can be settled.

tests.gap: The regression checks are read for shape only. Nothing runs them against a finished build.

tests.label: Skill files that point an agent at the method

tests.why: Each skill names only its own entry document.
Each skill tells the agent to read that document first.
Each skill resolves its paths against the installed clone.

tests.gap: The wording is checked. Nothing proves an agent given one of these files reaches the method.

tests.label: Public documents and the record of why

tests.why: Every reason entry parses and still points at a line that exists.
The record names no private project.
The public readme lists things in the order the tools use.

tests.gap: Almost nothing checks the public readme or the contributor guide. Both can go stale without failing.

tests.label: Coverage rows this table is made of

tests.why: Coverage rows reach the browser with their targets resolved to names.
A coverage row naming an invented id is refused.

tests.gap: Nothing checks that a coverage row's cited files exist. A stale citation ships quietly.

tests.label: Drawing libraries fetched from the internet

tests.why: Panning and zooming a picture is measured after the picture is painted.

tests.gap: Four libraries load from two outside services. No test covers a machine with no internet, where the viewer goes blank.

tests.label: Guarded places the map must not lose

tests.why: A file that lost its only access decision is named.
The closing verdict states the guarded places it found.
An access decision nobody voted on is called out.

tests.gap: Loss is measured against a stored earlier map. A guard missing from both maps stays invisible.
